summary: Little Mugget Hill lookout in Charlton: a 1917-18 tower lost to the 1938 hurricane, a 1939 CCC-built replacement, and a 2016 state listing of standing and active.

facts.design: 60-foot Aermotor steel tower with a 10x10-foot wood cab (registry); FFLA gives a 68-foot structure height
facts.agency: Massachusetts Bureau of Forest Fire Control

access.note: Mass.gov says state fire observation towers are not open to the general public; no visitor or rental information found for this tower.

events.note: Site first used for fire detection; watched from the ground in a grassy pasture until a tower went up
First tower: registry says 48 ft built 1917; 1917 state report says 50 ft; FFLA dates it 1918
Destroyed in the Great New England Hurricane, September 21, 1938
CCC-built replacement, 60-foot Aermotor steel tower with 10x10 wood cab; FFLA credits the US Forest Service with supplying it
New cab and chain link fence
Registered June 30, 2004 as US 587, MA 14; nominated by Henry Isenberg
State maintenance crew inspected the tower for possible future repair
State listing (last updated 5/8/2016) shows the tower standing and active

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Ground use from 1914 and the first tower of 1917 or 1918 are separate stages of one site; the 1939 CCC tower is the replacement the registry dates as built.

notes_for_editor: Disputed: first tower 1917 (registry, 1917 state report) vs 1918 (FFLA); height 48 ft (registry, FFLA) vs 50 ft (1917 state report); current tower 60 ft (registry, Forest Lookouts) vs 68 ft structure height (FFLA). FFLA credits the US Forest Service with supplying the 1939 tower. Elevation: registry 574 ft (175 m, matches the record) vs FFLA 1075 ft, which looks wrong, so it is not used. State tower number is 15 on the 2016 state listing and 26 on the FFLA page. Current access and rental are unverified; the only current signal is the 2016 listing and an undated FFLA page. A search summary claimed a 1951 68-foot replacement; no page I read supports it (the 68-foot 1949 line in the Forest Lookouts index sits under Deer Park Hill, Brewster), so it is not used. Ask the Bureau of Forest Fire Control to confirm current status and access before publishing any visit guidance. The 2015 report publisher is inferred from its firelookout.org host.
